newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CAPELLO BRACES HIMSELF FOR FANS' RAGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAPELLO BRACES HIMSELF FOR FANS' RAGE.

text.p: Rarely can a manager of a side with a league title virtually in the bag have dreaded a straightforward home game as much as Real Madrid's Fabio Capello must dread Sunday's fixture with Sporting Gijon.
Real fans are expected to use the game to vent their rage against the coach, who on Tuesday announced that he would leave the Spanish club at the end of the season.
The tension has already spilled over at training sessions, where supporters have shouted abuse at Capello.
Capello responded to two young fans by saying that he was more of a Real Madrid supporter than they were.
Earlier he had pledged his belief in the future of the team he has built.
"I'm sure that Real will win the league ... and the Champions' League," said the former AC Milan coach, who is widely rumoured to be on his way back to the struggling Italian champions.
The announcement, together with allegations made by Capello against the club board, sparked an angry reaction from Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz.
But with Real eight points clear at the top, Sanz swallowed his pride and agreed to continue working together with Capello until the end of the season.
Even so the instability created by the news is bound to affect the Real players.
Several commentators have blamed the upheaval for the poor showing of Real's Fernando Hierro and Raul Gonzalez in Spain's World Cup match with Yugoslavia on Wednesday.
And all-too-fresh in the minds of fans at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium will be the two league titles handed to arch-rivals Barcelona after defeats at Tenerife in the last game of successive seasons.
Real had squandered sizeable leads in both those campaigns, but with Capello in charge the team had looked far too solid a group to make the same mistakes again.
However the events of the past few days will remind fans that a week is a long time in football.
And anything but a win on Sunday could open the door to second-placed Barcelona.

Bobby Robson's side will know the Real result when they travel to lowly Extremadura on Monday, before hosting the leaders in the Camp Nou the following weekend in a clash that could yet prove decisive.
So Capello -- whose position looked enviable just five days ago -- is now faced with a situation that only the toughest men would relish.
Even so few who know the tough Italian master could doubt that it is also the kind of situation that promises to bring the best out of Capello.
